page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-2 is an entry-level virtual machine instance within the compute-optimized C2D family. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. The instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical CPU core via simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). It is equipped with 8.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU) alongside 32 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. The instance contains no integrated GPUs and has no local NVMe storage, meaning network-attached block storage must be provisioned separately. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread performance alongside bounded multi-threaded and memory throughput. In stress-ng single-core tests, the c2d-standard-2 achieved 2,923.48 (top 25%), complemented by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,620.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 27.81 GB/sec. However, multi-core scaling is strictly limited by the 2-vCPU ceiling: stress-ng multi-core reached 2,928.18 and Geekbench multi-core posted 2,021.0, both placing in the bottom 25%. Memory throughput measures 33.76 GB/sec read and 24.26 GB/sec write for large 256 MB blocks, ranking in the lower tiers alongside PassMark memory (1,012.47) and database operation tests (1,018.04).

Operating at the smallest footprint in the C2D series, this server trades overall concurrency for cost-effective dedicated per-core compute power. The absence of local storage and low memory bandwidth make it poorly matched for intensive databases, high-IOPS caches (Redis settled at 2.22 million SET ops/sec), or large parallel compilation jobs. Instead, the c2d-standard-2 fits single-threaded background jobs, microservices, lightweight web serving, and testing or development environments requiring steady x86_64 compute with modern cryptographic CPU instructions like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-2 is an entry-tier compute-optimized virtual machine featuring an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs sourced from 1 physical core with 2 threads, 8.0 GB of system memory, and a 32 MB L3 cache. The instance lacks local storage, GPUs, and complimentary IPv4 addresses, utilizing external storage options. Benchmark data demonstrates capable single-core execution, achieving a stress-ng single-core score of 2,923.48 and single-threaded gzip compression of 27.81 GB/sec. However, overall throughput is constrained by the small core count, with low memory bandwidth and multi-core metrics across Geekbench and PassMark. It offers an efficient entry point for dedicated x86_64 compute, suited for lightweight web serving, single-threaded batch tasks, small microservices, and general testing workloads.
